## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd5ad0e95aa8fae8a659796289b7d247aa917bad`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23048 (body and all eight comments, among them the decision analysis 6134774406, the ruling record 6135970276 with execution parameters (1)–(6) and the fork clause, the claim 6136107596 and the dev report 6136862799); PR #23129's body, file list and the net diff `origin/main...bd5ad0e95` (7 files, +585/−209); the check-runs on the head; reads of `origin/main` and the head with `git show` / `git grep`. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

**Check-runs on the head, read after the last shard completed (02:39Z): 45 runs — 34 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress.** The skips are the paths-filtered lanes (`Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the dogfood and temporal lanes gated on `filter.outputs.core`, the opt-in tarball smoke) and the duplicate labelled-event runs of Auto Label / Check PR Size / Check Changeset — none is this diff's failure; `Test Core` ran on `crosspkg`. Of the five required contexts, four are success and `Build Core` is skipped by its `filter.outputs.core` gate (no path under `packages/**` in the diff) — the by-design skip shape, not a red. Of note: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` ran the head's own guard code with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set and cleared on the pull_request leg — a live reading of `guardRepository` plus the threaded repository.

### ① Derived judgments

**The ruling's six execution steps and the fork clause (6135970276):**

- **(1) the scope key, default every repository, six rows untouched — RIGHT.** `repos` on the row; `surfaceRepos` is the one reader of the default (a row with no key governs every id in `GOVERNED_REPOS`); the six existing rows are byte-identical in the diff and keep their tiers; pinned by `the-six-pre-existing-rows-declare-no-scope-and-so-govern-every-repository` and `every-declared-scope-is-a-non-empty-duplicate-free-subset-of-GOVERNED_REPOS-ids` (so a `repos: []` row, which would govern nothing, is refused by the self-test).
- **(2) the matcher refuses a call without a repository, loudly — RIGHT.** `assertGovernedRepo` throws a `TypeError` naming the caller, the roster and the fix, on a missing id (`undefined`, `null`, `''`) and on an unknown one (a slug is refused with a pointer to `repoIdForSlug`); every front door asserts: `governedPathsIn`, `governedTierFor`, `testVerdict`, `classifyCommit`, `governedSurfacesFor`. Pinned in both directions, and the dev's ablation of the missing-repository branch turned the battery red.
- **(3) every caller passes its repository, no silent default to every repository anywhere — RIGHT.** Enumerated by `git grep` on the head, not from the report. merges: the sweep hands `classifyCommit` the `GOVERNED_REPOS` entry it iterates (line 4174); `--pr` resolves the slug it names and refuses one outside the register before any read; `--test` / `--branch` resolve the checkout at `--root` (`checkoutRepoFor`) and refuse a fork or no-origin checkout; `emitVerdict`'s default is `undefined`, which `testVerdict` refuses. queue guard: `main()` resolves `guardRepository(process.env)` BEFORE the diff is read and threads it through `liftGeneratedExceptions`, `runGuard`, `runSizeGuard`; `decomposeGovernedWork`, `guardVerdict`, `sizeReading`, `sizeGuardVerdict` all assert; the reader's slug is the same reading. half-states: `loadGovernedRegister(load, slug = OWNER_REPO)` binds the matcher ONCE to the swept board (`resolveSweepRepo(process.env)`), and a board outside the roster is `available: false` with the board named — NOT MEASURED, never judged against another repository's rows. prose gate: `governedSurfacesFor(SELF_REPO_ID)`. record-recognisers: both call sites. No other caller exists on the head: `dispatch-gates*.mjs` import only `GOVERNED_REPOS`, `SELF_REPO_ID`, `sizeVerdict`, `parseNumstat` and own a read-census roster their header says is not a copy of the register; `fleet-write/*` read `GOVERNED_REPOS` for slugs; no hook, workflow or package script spawns `--test`. The only defaults left are to ONE named repository, each printed or carried on the verdict: the guard's "this file's own" when `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is unset (a local run; Actions always sets it) and the patrol's `DEFAULT_SWEEP_REPO`. Neither is "all".
- **(4) the workflows row scoped to objectstack, objectui and cloud — RIGHT.** `prefix: '.github/workflows/'`, `glob: '.github/workflows/**'`, Tier H, `repos` exactly the three, cloud's table wording; pinned exactly, and the dev's ablation of the `repos` key turned five cases red.
- **(5) the named self-tests — RIGHT.** `an-objectos-workflow-path-is-NOT-governed`, `a-cloud-workflow-path-is-governed-Tier-H`, `⛔ no-repository-is-an-ERROR-never-an-answer-for-every-repository` are all in the merges battery, with hotcrm, objectui, the near misses (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**`, `.github/workflowsx/`, `packages/x/.github/workflows/`), `surfacesChecked` 7 vs 6, and the verdict carrying `repo`; the guard's battery adds the queue-level case (an unapproved workflow PR REFUSED at merge_group on the Tier H terminal, cleared on an authorized head approval) and every builder rejecting without a repository. Floors: battery pins 20 / 14 against 23 / 15 registered cases; rosters 32→33, 24→25.
- **(6) the docblock rewrite — WRONG BY OMISSION. This is the FAIL.** The `GOVERNED_SURFACES` docblock (the sentence the decision analysis cited at old lines 1126–1127) is rewritten as ruled, and so are the `testVerdict` docblock, the `--test` head line and the `parsePullTarget` docblock. But the same file's header — the authority on detail, per AGENTS.md — keeps, in its section "The governed REPOS" (head lines 543–546): "So the surface register above is REPO-AGNOSTIC: the same five surface globs are governed in `objectstack`, `objectui`, `cloud`, `objectos` and `hotcrm`, and this sweep covers all five repos in one invocation regardless of the working directory it is run from." Present tense, capitalised, stating exactly the claim B2 overturned, 420 lines below the new header section that states the opposite; and "regardless of the working directory" is now false for `--test` / `--branch`, which this very PR makes answer for the checkout at `--root`. The same header's tier table (lines 417–419) enumerates Tier H as "`docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` … Unchanged." and omits the new Tier H row the self-test pins (`Tier-H-is-the-law-…-and-the-workflows-row`). On `origin/main` the file had five non-test "repo-agnostic" sites; the dev rewrote the four lowercase ones and missed the capitalised one. An AI seat reading the header gets the pre-ruling answer. Fix (two docblock edits, no behaviour): rewrite 543–546 to the ruled shape (default every repository, a row may be scoped; the sweep still covers all five; `--test` / `--branch` answer for the checkout at `--root`), and name the workflows row in the Tier H line at 417–419 or replace that list with the complement rule 14 now uses.
- **The fork clause — RIGHT.** No caller was left unable to know its repository, so the clause did not fire and nothing defaulted to "all". `--test` / `--branch` take the checkout's `remote.origin.url` through `slugFromRemote` — the identical reading a bare `--pr N` already makes (lines 3723–3724) — and refuse when it parses to no governed repository.

**Fail-OPEN check — none found for objectstack, objectui or cloud.** Every matcher refuses without a repository; `--pr` refuses an unknown slug (exit 1, roster named); `--test` / `--branch` refuse an unknown or missing origin; the guard refuses an unknown `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` with `EXIT_CANNOT_RUN`; the patrol marks a foreign board NOT MEASURED; the generated-artifact lift asserts before it lifts; an unscoped row still governs every repository (pinned: AGENTS.md, ADRs and `.claude/**` still govern objectos and hotcrm). One misuse surface worth naming, not fail-open by the brief's definition: `--test` run from an objectos or hotcrm checkout against another repository's file list answers for that checkout (exit 0 on a workflow path). The stderr note names the repository judged and the `--root` remedy; the stale header sentence above is what would invite the misuse.

**The governed prose, true against the register after the change:**

- `AGENTS.md` rule 14, lines 266–268 — TRUE. The seven globs that govern objectstack are named as code spans and no other; `check:pm-governed-prose` reads the whole directive as its region and is green. The two cuts that paid for the glob ("the file you are reading is one" → "this file is one"; "on a single path hit" → "on one path hit") lose no meaning.
- `AGENTS.md` line 279, the Tier H parenthetical "(人合: every register row except `.claude/**`)" — TRUE today (Tier S is exactly the `claude-tree` row; the other six are H) and derivable from the rule alone: the enumeration three sentences up minus `.claude/**`. It says neither less nor more; what it trades away is self-containment, and the prose gate pins globs, not tiers, so a future Tier S row outside `.claude/**` would silently falsify it — where the explicit list would silently under-claim. Under the byte budget (the line was 117 bytes; the explicit list plus the seventh glob exceeds 120 and both files are at their line ceilings) the complement form is the right choice, and it matches what `SKILL.md:204` and `os-dev.md:286` already say. Listed for the maintainer below (dev deviation 7).
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` line 184 — TRUE; paid by dropping the spaces around `+`, 「(全量)」 kept, 120 bytes.
- `SKILL.md` line 185 — RIGHT to rewrite, and in scope: 「`GOVERNED_REPOS` 各仓同治理待遇」 (every repository receives the same treatment) became false the moment one row is scoped; 「同治理、行可限仓」 states the new shape without over- or under-claiming. The in-place conditions (`review-checklist.md:25`, `os-dev.md:68`) hold: same defect class (prose against the register), mechanical, no other claim on the file, same gate family. Terse, not misreadable.

**The dev's deviations:**

- `record-recognisers.mjs` edited beyond the claimed surface — RIGHT: it calls the re-exported `governedTierFor` and `runGuard`, whose signatures changed; it is a caller under (3), and `check:pm-record-recognisers` would throw without the edit. Declared in the body and the report.
- `SKILL.md` line 185 rewritten — RIGHT (above).
- `--root` instead of a `--repo` flag — RIGHT: the file's closed-argv section records "There is no `--repo` here, by ruling — one spelling"; a flag would reopen the argv with a second spelling, while `--root` already exists and its origin is the reading a bare `--pr N` makes. It is a behaviour change to a seat-facing predicate (a fork or no-origin checkout now refuses `--test` where it used to answer), in the fail-closed direction; listed for the maintainer.
- The queue guard has no `--test` — RIGHT: confirmed by grep (no `--test` parsing; it reads `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` only). The card's acceptance line conflated the two tools; the merges predicate answers GOVERNED Tier H and the guard's own battery pins the workflow case at the queue. Inventing a flag would be scope.

Also judged: the `--test` head line now reads "(7 surfaces govern objectstack)" and the `--json` verdict gains `repo` — no consumer on the head parses the old line or `surfacesChecked` (`git grep`), so nothing downstream breaks; `check-governed-prose` demanding only the rows that govern `SELF_REPO_ID` is right (this repository's prose must not claim a surface governed only elsewhere); the three untouched `--test` doc sites (`references/lanes/skills.md:17`, `references/state-machine.md:9`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs:28`) stay true because a seat runs the predicate in the checkout of the PR's repository.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` matches what the diff publishes: nothing. The seven files are repo-root `scripts/pm/**`, `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/**`; no path under `packages/**`, no published export, no authorable key. `Check Changeset` is green. `Clause-②: no` is right — the changed function signatures are internal tooling contracts, documented in the PR body, not a metadata or API surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none — accepted; the fork clause did not fire.
- Dev deviations (1)–(4): judged RIGHT above. (5) the harness `Co-Authored-By` trailer refused by the pre-push hook, the commits carrying the repository's model-free pair — correct. (6) building `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` so gate 23 could measure — a prerequisite, not a change. (7) the complement form on line 279 — the maintainer's call, below. (8) writes through the fleet relay, read back — fine.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, each correctly out: #1 `parsePullTarget` accepting any slug — verified that `--pr` refuses a slug outside the register before any read (head lines 3736–3745), so no silent answer exists. #2 `governed-surface-guard.yml` has no `paths:` filter (verified) and `dispatch-gates.mjs` names a register row only in a comment table (6857), its read-census rosters (9148–9149) being, by its own header, not a copy of the register. #3 `AGENTS.md` has 14 lines over 120 bytes (table rows); the ratchet governs edited lines of its covered files, and `check:pm-skill-ratchet` is green.
- Reviewer's own, not filed (read-only seat), for the owning seat to carry: the pm-dispatch lane table now has one path under two rows — `SKILL.md:165` gives `domain:skills` "governed 面全量(统一定义见「governed 面统一定义」行)", which after line 184 includes `.github/workflows/**`, while `SKILL.md:164` still routes `.github/workflows/`(接线) to `domain:spec` by the anchoring exception. Both sentences are now true of a workflow PR; a follow-up card on the lane table, not this PR.
- Tier H is not lifted by this record: the PR has 0 reviews; it stays a draft until a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account approves, and the record for the fixed head must be rendered first.

**What the maintainer must look at** (after the fix push and a fresh PASS record):

1. Rule 14 line 279: the Tier H parenthetical moved from an explicit list to "every register row except `.claude/**`" under the byte budget — explicit list or complement is your call (dev deviation 7).
2. `check-governed-merges.mjs --test` / `--branch` now answer for the checkout at `--root` (its `origin` resolved to a register id, printed on stderr) and refuse a fork or no-origin checkout; there is no `--repo` flag, per the file's closed-argv ruling.
3. The lane-table overlap on `.github/workflows/**` (`SKILL.md` 164 vs 165) — a follow-up card for the skills seat, if you want workflow PRs routed one way.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23048-workflows-governed`
Reviewed-by: `session_012dGTuJen61ECNHXYXKChoC`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 维护者速读(终稿)

PR #23129 · card #23048 · head `27902d268` · seat `domain:skills#2` (`session_012dGTuJen61ECNHXYXKChoC`), written 2026-10-13T03:12Z. The seat checked the dev's draft against the diff it read; this comment is the version to read.

**改了什么(按你裁的 B2)**
- 受管面登记表 `GOVERNED_SURFACES` 的每一行可以带一个「适用仓」栏 `repos`。不写就是五个仓全管,原有六行一字未改、档位不变。
